svg.text: Orange Pi Water Logger Wiring Diagram
Zero 3 header shown. For Orange Pi 5 Max, map the same 5V, GND, 3.3V, I2C, UART, and optional ready functions to its enabled header pins.
GND out to Orange Pi GND
1 Power bank 5V to Pico VSYS/USB and 5V power-switch input
2 Power bank GND to common GND bus (Pico, switch, Orange Pi, all sensor modules)
3 Pico GP15 to 5V power-switch TRIG / EN
4 Pico GP14 to momentary button NO (button C to common GND)
8 5V power-switch output to Orange Pi 5V input
9 5V power-switch ground out to Orange Pi GND
10 Orange Pi 3.3V to ADS1115 #1 VDD, ADS1115 #2 VDD, DS18B20 VCC, BME280 VCC
11 Orange Pi SDA to ADS1115 #1 SDA, ADS1115 #2 SDA, BME280 SDA
12 Orange Pi SCL to ADS1115 #1 SCL, ADS1115 #2 SCL, BME280 SCL
13 Orange Pi pin 7 (PC9 / GPIO7) to DS18B20 DATA (with 4.7k pull-up to 3.3V)
14-19 Sensor analogs: pH/TDS/turbidity/ORP to ADS1 A0/A1/A2/A3; DO/NH4+ ISE to ADS2 A0/A1 22 OPi UART TX to Pico GP1 24 Pico GP0/TX to OPi UART RX 25 Optional ready GPIO
- Every block above is a physically separate module.
- Do not power the Orange Pi from a Pico GPIO pin.
- Pico GP15 drives only the relay/MOS switch trigger input.
- ADS1115 #1 ADDR to GND (0x48); ADS1115 #2 ADDR to 3.3V (0x49).
- ADS1115 analog inputs must stay between 0V and 3.3V. Add a
voltage divider if a sensor board can output above 3.3V.
- The UART interval link (#22, #24) is required for adaptive logging.
- Optional ready GPIO (#25) lets the Pico cut power sooner after
the Orange Pi has shut down.
green GPIO control / UART blue / purple I2C SDA / SCL
